name: Void-Anchor
description: Void-Anchor earned its name from the gravitational anomalies that dot its surface, regions where gravity inexplicably intensifies to crushing levels or reverses entirely, creating permanent pillars of floating debris. The planet itself is massive for a barren world, its high gravity making surface operations exhausting even for enhanced personnel. Canyon systems carved by ancient water cut kilometers deep into the crust, revealing strata that tell a story of geological violence stretching back billions of years.

The heavy gravity presses down with tangible weight, every movement requiring conscious effort, every task taking longer than it would elsewhere. The thin atmosphere offers no relief, lungs working harder to extract sufficient oxygen while muscles strain against the planetary pull. Yet people come to Void-Anchor despite the hardship, drawn by what lies beneath its hostile surface and what orbits above.

The defense platforms circling Void-Anchor are not human construction, their automated systems responding to queries in no known language, their weapons tracking any vessel that approaches without authorization. Somehow, certain approach vectors trigger acceptance rather than targeting—a code or frequency that someone, somewhere, figured out through trial and fatal error. The platforms guard the megastructure buried beneath the largest gravity well, a facility that may hold the key to artificial gravity manipulation or the extinction of anyone foolish enough to activate it.

Research into the buried structure proceeds with extreme caution, each chamber assessed for traps before entry, each artifact analyzed remotely before handling. The civilization that built this place understood gravity at a fundamental level, manipulating it as casually as humans manipulate electricity. Their fate remains unknown—the facility shows no signs of violent end, simply abandonment, as if the builders completed their purpose and departed. What that purpose was, and whether it's finished or simply waiting, keeps researchers working despite the crushing weight that never relents.
